messages:
maya (Sales): Need a concise SIG/CAIQ-ready answer for encryption and KMS for procurement. They want specifics for in-transit, at-rest, BYOK/HSM, rotation, and whether keys ever leave customer accounts.
li (Solutions Eng): Draft: TLS 1.3 for all network traffic. At-rest AES-256-GCM. Envelope encryption where DEKs are wrapped by CMKs. Support for customer-provided CMKs via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault. For Private deployments we can integrate with on-prem HSMs (KMIP/PKCS#11) and accept vendor attestation. Redwood never stores plaintext master keys.
asha (Security): Add audit wording: all key operations (wrap/unwrap/rotate) are logged to immutable audit trails. Audit exports available in the compliance pack. For BYOK with customer KMS, keys stay in the customer's cloud account; Redwood only receives wrapped DEKs.
jon (Prospect IT): Important: "keys stay in customer's account" needs explicit wording for procurement. Also they require HSM attestation (L3) evidence. Can you provide the exact sentence?
li (Solutions Eng): Use this sentence: "When customers supply a CMK in their cloud account, Redwood does not export or extract the CMK; only wrapped DEKs are transmitted to Redwood. For Private/on-prem deployments Redwood can integrate with customer HSMs; FIPS/attestation artifacts are provided by the HSM vendor and included in the compliance pack."
asha (Security): Add note on default behavior: hosted accounts default to Redwood-managed provider keys (we'll document which provider region/account). Dedicated/Private customers can opt into BYOK or HSM integrations so keys remain under customer control.
maya (Sales): They also asked about rotation cadence options (90/180/365) and emergency rotation.
li (Solutions Eng): Rotation options: 1) Customer-managed: rotate in their KMS and update the CMK reference; 2) Redwood-managed rewrap: Redwood can perform scheduled DEK rewraps and coordinate CMK version updates (typical configurable cadence: 90/180/365). Emergency forced rotation supported via incident runbook; will trigger rolling rewrap and validation windows. No plaintext master keys are ever persisted.
jon (Prospect IT): For HSM integration: do you generate keys in our HSM or can you accept externally generated keys with attestation? We need attested key generation.
asha (Security): We can accept externally-generated keys with vendor attestation. If we generate keys on behalf of customer, that's a special engagement and we need documented controls and audit scope. For standard Private deployments we recommend keys be generated and remain in-custody with the customer's HSM.
li (Solutions Eng): POC note: typical timeline for HSM hookup is ~2-4 weeks including network, key sync, and attestation verification. We'll need network allowlist, KMIP endpoint, and someone from the customer's infra to coordinate.
maya (Sales): Can we give them a short SIG-style paragraph for the questionnaire?
asha (Security): Suggested SIG line: "Redwood enforces TLS 1.3 for data-in-transit and AES-256-GCM for data-at-rest. We use envelope encryption with DEKs encrypted by customer-managed or provider-managed CMKs. Customers may provide CMKs via supported cloud KMS or integrate HSM-backed keys for Private deployments; key operations are audited and attestation artifacts from HSM vendors are provided as part of the compliance pack. Redwood does not export customer CMKs."
li (Solutions Eng): I'll add an example AWS KMS snippet to the presales repo so procurement can see the ARN style.
deploy-bot: Presales template updated: https://redwood.internal/sales/presales-crypto (view changelog)
maya (Sales): Great — action items: li to add example config + POC checklist; asha to attach audit excerpts and attestation checklist; I'll send the SIG paragraph to procurement.
jon (Prospect IT): Thanks all. I'll route this to legal and the security team. If they need the HSM vendor attestation, I'll request it after legal OKs. :thumbsup:
